Trend extraction with Fourier seasonality for weekly series

Source: R/trend_index.R
extract_trend.Rd

Splits each weekly series (one per key) into a deterministic annual seasonal component, a trend and a remainder, on a transformed scale (log for totals, logit for shares). The seasonal component is a Fourier regression whose number of harmonics is chosen by AICc and estimated jointly with the trend by backfitting.

Usage

extract_trend(
  dt,
  key_cols,
  time_col,
  value_col,
  transform = c("log", "logit", "none"),
  method = c("llt", "smooth", "ets", "stl"),
  period = 365.25/7,
  harmonics = NULL,
  max_harmonics = 6L,
  n_backfit = 3L,
  level = 0.95
)

Arguments

dt

A data.frame or data.table with one row per key x week.

key_cols

Character vector of key columns identifying each series.

time_col

Name of the time column (class Date or IDate, weekly).

value_col

Name of the value column (positive for log, in (0, 1) for logit); NA allowed.

transform

Scale of the model: "log", "logit" or "none".

method

Trend method: "llt" (default), "smooth" (local linear trend with level variance fixed at zero), "ets" or "stl".

period

Seasonal period in weeks (default 365.25 / 7).

harmonics

Fixed number of Fourier harmonics, or NULL to choose it by AICc. Ignored by stl.

max_harmonics

Largest number of harmonics considered when harmonics = NULL.

n_backfit

Number of backfitting iterations (non-negative integer).

level

Confidence level of trend_lo and trend_hi (llt and smooth only).

Value

A data.table with columns key_cols, time_col (IDate), observed (transformed scale, NA for missing weeks), seasonal, trend (smoothed for llt), trend_filtered, trend_se, trend_lo, trend_hi, remainder (observed - seasonal - trend), imputed (logical, TRUE where the input was missing) and method, ordered by key and time. Attribute fits: one row per key with method, K, aicc, var_level, var_slope, var_obs, convergence, zero_variance, fixed_variance, boundary, retried, start, degenerate, interpolated, n_obs, n_na and error. Attributes transform, key_cols, time_col and period record the call.

Details

Grid and missing weeks. Within each key, times must be on a weekly grid; missing weeks (absent rows or NA values, e.g. outlier weeks set to NA upstream) are kept as NA in observed and flagged in imputed. The trend at those weeks is the model prediction (llt, smooth) or comes from a linear interpolation of the input used for fitting (ets, stl); the per-key flag interpolated in the fits attribute marks the latter.

Seasonality. For llt, smooth and ets, the seasonal component is \(s_t = \sum_{k=1}^K a_k \sin(2\pi k t/P) + b_k \cos(2\pi k t/P)\), with t the number of weeks since 1970-01-01 (so the phase is common to all keys) and P = period. When harmonics = NULL, K ranges over 0..max_harmonics and is chosen by \(AICc = -2\ell + 2p + 2p(p+1)/(n-p-1)\), where \(\ell\) is the log-likelihood of the trend model on the seasonally adjusted series and p counts the trend parameters plus 2K seasonal coefficients. The backfitting starts from an OLS fit of a quadratic time trend plus the harmonics, then n_backfit times fits the trend on y - s and regresses y - trend on the harmonics; a final trend fit on the last adjusted series gives the output.

Methods.

  • llt (reference): local linear trend, stats::StructTS(type = "trend") on the adjusted series. trend is the smoothed (two-sided) level from stats::KalmanSmooth(), trend_se its smoothed standard deviation, trend_filtered the filtered (one-sided) level. NA weeks are handled by the Kalman filter.

  • smooth: smooth trend model, the local linear trend of llt with the level disturbance variance fixed at zero (stats::StructTS(type = "trend", fixed = c(0, NA, NA)), parameters in the order level, slope, epsilon). The level then has no shocks of its own and the trend is an integrated random walk: only the slope changes from week to week. Its smoothed level is a cubic-spline-type smoother whose smoothness is set by the signal-to-noise ratio q = var_slope / var_obs, estimated by maximum likelihood (no smoothing parameter is chosen by hand). Smoothing, trend_se, optimiser starts and treatment of NA weeks are those of llt; var_level is reported as 0 and fixed_variance as "level".

  • ets: fable::ETS(error("A") + trend(c("A", "Ad")) + season("N")) on the adjusted series, with NA weeks linearly interpolated (ETS does not accept missing values). trend and trend_filtered are both the filtered level; trend_se is NA. Requires tsibble, fable and fabletools.

  • stl: stats::stl(s.window = "periodic", robust = TRUE) with frequency 52 on the interpolated series. It has its own periodic seasonal component (no Fourier terms, K = NA) and a 52-week period instead of 52.18: a descriptive benchmark only.

Boundary estimates and failed fits. A variance estimated at zero is a legitimate boundary maximum-likelihood estimate, not a failure: a zero slope variance means a deterministic drift, a zero level variance an integrated random walk (smooth) trend, a zero observation variance a series without measurement noise (e.g. a moving sum). For llt and smooth, zero_variance lists the estimated variances at zero (below 1e-8 times the variance of the first differences) and boundary is TRUE when there is at least one; the level variance of smooth is fixed by the model, not estimated, so it is listed in fixed_variance and never in zero_variance or boundary; for ets, zero_variance lists the smoothing parameters (alpha, beta) at their lower bound 1e-4 and boundary flags them. The llt (and smooth) likelihood is maximised from two starts: the StructTS default and the series rescaled to unit standard deviation of its first differences, with initial variances (level 0.5, slope 0.01, observation 0.5) on that scale and an optimiser parscale of 0.01 for the slope variance; the variances are back-transformed. The default start alone often stops at a spurious zero slope variance with a lower likelihood. Among the converged starts (convergence == 0, finite log-likelihood) the one with the highest log-likelihood is kept (start); retried is TRUE when the default start did not converge. When neither start converges and the best one has variances at zero, the model is refitted with those variances fixed at zero (start = "boundary"); the refit is kept when it converges without loss of likelihood, which confirms a boundary maximum. degenerate marks failed fits only: for llt, when no start converges (the best finite one is then returned). Leading missing weeks are excluded from the estimation (StructTS needs an observed first value) and filled by the Kalman smoother. For ets, degenerate marks a non-finite log-likelihood. No fallback method is used: when a fit errors (e.g. on a deterministic series), the key keeps NA components, degenerate is TRUE, the message is stored in error and a warning is raised.

Uncertainty. trend_se (and trend_lo, trend_hi) is the model-based standard error of the smoothed level, conditional on the estimated variances and seasonal coefficients. It is valid only when the observed series is not itself a moving sum: for stock-type series (moving sums of inflow, such as the stock of open postings), the innovations are moving averages by construction and trend_se understates the uncertainty. Use it on inflow-type series only.

Cost. With harmonics = NULL, each key requires (max_harmonics + 1) * (n_backfit + 1) trend fits (each with two optimiser starts for llt and smooth). The AICc counts 3 trend parameters for llt and 2 for smooth.

Examples

set.seed(1)
weeks <- data.table::as.IDate("2023-05-01") + 7L * (0:155)
tw <- as.numeric(weeks) / 7
d <- data.table::data.table(
  source = "a",
  week = weeks,
  n = exp(5 + 0.003 * seq_along(weeks) +
    0.2 * sin(2 * pi * tw / (365.25 / 7)) + rnorm(156, 0, 0.03))
)
tr <- extract_trend(d, "source", "week", "n", max_harmonics = 2L)
head(tr)
#>    source       week observed   seasonal    trend trend_filtered    trend_se

#> 2:      a 2023-05-08 5.175483 0.16846276 4.991509       4.998774 0.000780673
#> 3:      a 2023-05-15 5.132962 0.15395670 4.995264       4.990640 0.001014808
#> 4:      a 2023-05-22 5.191788 0.13722092 4.999014       5.021635 0.001235456
#> 5:      a 2023-05-29 5.137803 0.11849782 5.002755       5.025673 0.001443171
#> 6:      a 2023-06-05 5.085656 0.09805854 5.006486       5.017155 0.001638417
#>    trend_lo trend_hi    remainder imputed method
#>       <num>    <num>        <num>  <lgcl> <char>
#> 1: 4.984540 4.990956 -0.007528133   FALSE    llt
#> 2: 4.989979 4.993039  0.015512034   FALSE    llt

#> 5: 4.999926 5.005583  0.016550324   FALSE    llt
#> 6: 5.003275 5.009698 -0.018888662   FALSE    llt
attr(tr, "fits")
#>    source method     K      aicc var_level    var_slope      var_obs
#>    <char> <char> <int>     <num>     <num>        <num>        <num>
#> 1:      a    llt     1 -648.7773         0 6.098826e-09 0.0007024439
#>    convergence zero_variance fixed_variance boundary retried    start
#>          <int>        <char>         <char>   <lgcl>  <lgcl>   <char>
#> 1:           0         level                    TRUE   FALSE rescaled
#>    degenerate interpolated n_obs  n_na  error
#>        <lgcl>       <lgcl> <int> <int> <char>
#> 1:      FALSE        FALSE   156     0   <NA>
# smooth trend model: level variance fixed at 0
ts_ <- extract_trend(d, "source", "week", "n", method = "smooth",
  harmonics = 1L)
attr(ts_, "fits")[, c("var_level", "var_slope", "var_obs", "fixed_variance")]
